goal.text: The wearer is hunting through the house for something she cannot find, and wants to know which places she has already searched and which she has not.

turns.text: What have I taken off that shelf so far?

trigger.detail: nothing has been asked yet in this window

expected_answer.text: Only a tea sachet. You picked one up, set it back down on the container, and then took a different one.

turns.text: Both hands, or just the one?

trigger.detail: user cuts in while the count is being read back

expected_answer.text: Right hand for both grabs. Your left only came in once you had straightened up with it.

turns.text: So nothing got left behind back there?

trigger.detail: gaze leaves the first shelf as she turns away

expected_answer.text: Nothing of yours. The first one you handled went back onto the container, and the container stays put.

turns.text: oh — by the way, which hand did I just free up?

trigger.detail: box comes down off the wall mounted shelf

expected_answer.text: Your left. You parked what you were carrying up on the wall mounted shelf and brought the box down with your right.

turns.text: Right, and did I get what I wanted out of it?

trigger.detail: the box is opened, emptied and closed again

expected_answer.text: Yes. You opened it, drew a second sachet out with your left hand, then shut it and put it back up there.

turns.text: And the first one? Did that go back?

trigger.detail: cuts in before the answer finishes

expected_answer.text: It did. You swapped them between hands on the way over and dropped the older one back on the container.

turns.text: What have I got in my hands right now?

trigger.detail: she stops walking and stands at the kitchen table

expected_answer.text: One sachet, torn open. You are working the tea bag out of it with your left hand as you stand there.

turns.text: mm-hm... mm— actually, how long have I been at this?

trigger.detail: a backchannel turns into a question

expected_answer.text: About fifty seconds since you first bent down in the dining area. Most of it was walking between the two shelves.

turns.text: Right — hot water next. Am I set up for that?

trigger.detail: mug reaches the counter and the kettle is lifted

expected_answer.text: You are. It is on the counter with the bag in it, and the kettle is already up in your right hand.

turns.text: wait — where has the little tag gone?

trigger.detail: gaze leaves the plant for the counter top while pouring

expected_answer.text: Still pinched in your left hand along with the mug. Your right is fully taken up with pouring.

turns.text: Hm. And now I am at the sink. What for?

trigger.detail: she turns and stops in front of the kitchen sink

expected_answer.text: You are running the drinking faucet into your drink, and you shut the faucet off again with your right hand.

turns.text: So it was not full enough off the kettle?

trigger.detail: cuts in to draw an inference

expected_answer.text: Looks that way. You only poured for a couple of seconds before you straightened back up.

turns.text: Have I actually drunk any of it yet?

trigger.detail: a quiet stretch with no new object handled

expected_answer.text: Two mouthfuls so far. One as you turned from the sink, another after you walked a few steps forward.

turns.text: sorry, quick one — am I still carrying that wrapper around?

trigger.detail: an unrelated worry surfaces mid answer

expected_answer.text: No. You put it down on the table when you fished the bag out, and it has sat there since.

turns.text: Did it go back in the same spot?

trigger.detail: the mug is set down with both hands

expected_answer.text: Same surface, yes. Both hands, right in front of where you had been standing and talking.

turns.text: And I have picked the wrapper back up, have I not?

trigger.detail: cuts in to confirm

expected_answer.text: You have, in your right hand, while you were gesturing with both of them at your peers.

turns.text: Right. Did I manage that lid on my own?

trigger.detail: the sachet goes into the bin

expected_answer.text: No. One of your peers reached in and held the cover open for you before you could drop it in.

turns.text: um, hang on — which hand was holding it when it went in?

trigger.detail: cuts in for a detail about the same moment

expected_answer.text: Your left. Your right stayed up on the bin the whole time, even with the help you were given.

turns.text: Back to the drink. Same hand as last time?

trigger.detail: she lifts the mug off the table again

expected_answer.text: No. You lifted it with your right this time, where before you were always cradling it in two.

turns.text: And before that? Two, surely.

trigger.detail: cuts in to finish the comparison

expected_answer.text: Two every time. This is the first one handed lift of the whole stretch.

turns.text: I keep checking my watch. How often so far?

trigger.detail: a second wrist check as she walks on

expected_answer.text: Twice in about six seconds, and on different arms. Right wrist first, then the left one as you turned.

turns.text: no, I mean — across everything you have watched, not just now.

trigger.detail: the user repairs the scope of their own question

expected_answer.text: Then twice is still the whole count. Those are the only checks since you first bent down for a sachet.

turns.text: New room. What did I look out of?

trigger.detail: the curtain is released and she turns away

expected_answer.text: The little window in the laundry door. You held its curtain aside with your right hand and swayed to see out.

turns.text: And now I am pointing at something. What?

trigger.detail: cuts in on the next gesture

expected_answer.text: At a door, with your left hand, a moment before you turned and reached for its handle with that same hand.

turns.text: Two of them, or did I repeat?

trigger.detail: she walks out of the second bathroom

expected_answer.text: Two separate ones. You stepped into the first, turned straight around, and went into another beside it.

turns.text: actually — did I even look at anything in there?

trigger.detail: cuts in to ask about gaze rather than route

expected_answer.text: One thing. Your gaze went to the vanity top on the way out and you kept it there from the doorway.

turns.text: Bedroom now. Did I check both of those drawers?

trigger.detail: gaze leaves the wall and settles on the bedside table

expected_answer.text: Both, one straight after the other. Left hand for the upper, right hand for the lower while still gripping the upper.

turns.text: But I stepped over something on the way in. What was that?

trigger.detail: cuts in to resume an earlier moment

expected_answer.text: A vent in the floor. You trod on it, then crouched and hovered a hand over it before moving along.

turns.text: I have done those two again, have I not?

trigger.detail: the same pair of drawers is opened and shut a second time

expected_answer.text: You have. Same pair, this time right hand for both, and you pushed each of them shut with two hands.

turns.text: hold on — am I just going round in circles here?

trigger.detail: cuts in with a worry about the search itself

expected_answer.text: Somewhat. That was a second pass over ground you had covered, and nothing new has been opened since.

turns.text: Different room, same furniture. Is this one new to me?

trigger.detail: a drawer is opened in the second bedroom

expected_answer.text: New. You crossed the hallway into a second bedroom, and this is the first thing you have pulled open in here.

turns.text: And that is both of them in here too, now?

trigger.detail: cuts in to confirm the pair

expected_answer.text: Yes. The upper with both hands, the lower with just your right, and a wrist check in between the two.

turns.text: And over here, what is taking my weight?

trigger.detail: she straightens up from the desk

expected_answer.text: A chair. Your left hand is down on its armrest while your right works the drawers under the desk.

turns.text: uh, wait — there was a lid I opened just then too, was there not?

trigger.detail: the storage box cover is opened and closed

expected_answer.text: There was. You bent down and lifted the top cover of a storage box with both hands, then shut it again.

turns.text: I'm at a window again. The same one?

trigger.detail: the curtain is lifted open a second time

expected_answer.text: No, a third. One at the laundry door, one beside the bed, and now this one across the room from it.

turns.text: And I pointed out of it. With which hand?

trigger.detail: cuts in on the gesture

expected_answer.text: Left. The right stayed clamped on the curtain the whole time you were pointing and talking.

turns.text: Where did my eyes go first in here?

trigger.detail: gaze drops from the counter to the drawer she is pulling

expected_answer.text: Straight down onto the one you were pulling open. You looked off the surface above it as you bent over.

turns.text: sorry to interrupt — am I using one hand down here or two?

trigger.detail: cuts in about handedness

expected_answer.text: The right one only, for every drawer so far. Your left has hung at your side since you came in.

turns.text: Cupboards as well now. How did I do those?

trigger.detail: both cabinet doors are opened and closed

expected_answer.text: One door per hand, the pair of them together, and then you stepped left and went back to pulling with your right.

turns.text: So nothing has turned up yet, in any of them?

trigger.detail: cuts in for a running verdict

expected_answer.text: Nothing. You have opened and shut every one of them without taking a single item out.

turns.text: What is beside me that I cannot see?

trigger.detail: gaze lifts from the cabinets to the blank wall

expected_answer.text: Only the toilet, over on your side. It has been in frame since you came in and it drops out about now.

turns.text: no no — further back than that. What have I not checked at all?

trigger.detail: the user repairs the reach of their own question

expected_answer.text: The kitchen. You have opened nothing there since you left with your drink, and the dining shelves are untouched.

turns.text: What did my eyes land on coming through?

trigger.detail: gaze leaves the wall and holds on the couch

expected_answer.text: The couch, for a good four seconds, and you lifted a cushion off it and put it straight back down.

turns.text: And I reached for something on my left after that?

trigger.detail: cuts in on the gesture that followed

expected_answer.text: Towards the fridge, yes. Your left hand went up at it without ever actually touching it.

turns.text: Long gap there. Am I back to opening things?

trigger.detail: gaze comes off the couch onto a low table as she crouches

expected_answer.text: You are, with your left this time because your drink is in the right. You raised something inside and set it back.

turns.text: oh, before I forget — is that the first thing I have actually lifted out?

trigger.detail: cuts in to check the running tally

expected_answer.text: It is. Everywhere else you opened and closed without raising anything, so that was the first item handled.

turns.text: Still nothing. What are my hands doing now?

trigger.detail: gaze comes off the table as she listens

expected_answer.text: Only holding your drink, in both. You sipped twice and then stepped forward while your peer was talking.

turns.text: And my eyes? Still on them, or wandering?

trigger.detail: cuts in about gaze

expected_answer.text: Wandering. Your gaze slid off the surface it had been resting on and settled on a bare stretch of wall.

turns.text: Right, I am giving up. Where have I not looked?

trigger.detail: the search has run the length of the clip

expected_answer.text: Only the kitchen cupboards, and you have one of those open right now. Everywhere else you have been through.

turns.text: So that is everywhere, and it never turned up.

trigger.detail: gaze comes off the wall onto the cupboard she is closing

expected_answer.text: That is everywhere. Nothing you raised today was it, and the last one just shut on you empty.
